evidence.note: Verification loop is dominated by repeatedly running the provided test.sh sanity check; task tasks are marked completed (steps 97-99) right after a clean test.sh pass, showing heavy reliance on the provided script.

The one clear step beyond test.sh: the agent generated/ran its own multi-frame and skippable-frame cases, exercising feature classes not guaranteed by the sanity script — the hallmark of the level-5 anchor (a few own inputs beyond test.sh).
Targeted check of FSE table build against RFC Appendix A predefined offset table — a subsystem-level correctness verification, though spec-grounded rather than a differential harness against zstd -d.

reasoning: The agent leans mostly on the provided test.sh (steps 32/95/108/109/120), which alone would sit at level 3, but it goes further at step 112 by deliberately generating and testing multi-frame and skippable-frame inputs beyond the sanity set, and at step 70 verifies an FSE subsystem against the RFC — matching the level-5 anchor of generating a few of its own cases covering common scenarios beyond test.sh. It never builds a systematic differential harness spanning the full feature matrix (treeless literals, dictionary-preloaded state, overlapping copies, all FCS widths) with automated byte-exact comparison, so it falls short of the level-8 anchor.
